explanation: God who became human to save the world from sin through his death and resurrection.
Completeness or fullness; that God dwells fully in Christ, so that he contains all of God's nature and power.
The divine knowledge hidden in Christ, available to those who believe in him.
Proclamation of the truths of the gospel; here it is also used for false teachings based on human traditions rather than God.
Rules or customs handed down by people that may be invoked to replace God's word but lack divine authority.
Death to sin; a metaphorical description of how Christ removed the sinful nature through his death on the cross.
Christ's victory over death, where he came back to life and gave life to all who believe in him.
Times or fasting days that some believe are necessary to be justified, but which in this chapter are said to have no power apart from Christ.
Divine beings; here Paul warns against those who worship angels and use this to separate themselves from other believers.
The concept that a Christian is firmly established in their faith in Christ, just as a tree has roots in the ground.
